summary: Namibia keeps visa-free entry for SADC citizens and reciprocating states, but since April 1, 2025 it charges previously-exempt countries without reciprocity — including most EU states, the US, UK, Canada and Japan — a visa on arrival of NAD 1,600, obtainable at the border or online in advance.

payments.text: Cards are widely accepted in Windhoek, Swakopmund and at lodges; carry cash for fuel stops, small towns and park gates on long self-drive routes. South African rand are legal tender at 1:1 alongside the Namibian dollar.

safety.text: Namibia is one of southern Africa's safer countries. Petty theft occurs in Windhoek, but the biggest real risks are on the road — long gravel distances, punctures, and wildlife or livestock on the road at dusk.

bestTimeToVisit.text: The May–October dry winter is prime time: mild days, cold desert nights and superb wildlife viewing at Etosha's waterholes. Summer (November–April) brings heat and occasional rain that greens the landscape.

tips.text: Most touring routes are gravel — keep speeds under about 80 km/h, rent a car with two spare tires for long routes, and never drive at night when kudu and other wildlife cross the roads.

Namibia's entry rules changed on April 1, 2025 — many nationalities that used to enter free (EU states, US, UK, Canada, Japan and others) now pay NAD 1,600 for a visa on arrival. Check your status shortly before travel, as the lists may still be adjusted.
South African rand are accepted everywhere at 1:1, but Namibian dollars are not accepted back in South Africa — spend or change them before leaving.
Children under 18 should travel with a full (unabridged) birth certificate, and a consent affidavit from any parent not traveling — the same regime South Africa applies.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Namibia?
faq.answer: It changed in 2025. SADC citizens and nationals of countries that waive visas for Namibians still enter visa-free. But since April 1, 2025, citizens of 30-plus previously-exempt countries — including most EU states, the US, UK, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and Japan — must obtain a visa, available on arrival or online in advance for NAD 1,600 (about USD 90).

faq.question: How does Namibia's visa on arrival work?
faq.answer: Eligible nationals simply present their passport at the airport or a major land border, pay NAD 1,600 (about USD 90) by card or cash, and receive a visa allowing a stay of up to 90 days. To skip lines you can pre-apply through the Ministry of Home Affairs eServices portal.

faq.question: Who can still enter Namibia visa-free?
faq.answer: Citizens of SADC countries (South Africa, Botswana, Zambia, Zimbabwe, Angola and the rest) and of states that reciprocate Namibia's waiver — for example Russia, Singapore and Malaysia — continue to enter without a visa, typically for up to 90 days. Confirm your status before travel as the lists are periodically reviewed.

faq.question: Do children need extra documents to enter Namibia?
faq.answer: Yes — travelers under 18 should carry a full (unabridged) birth certificate alongside their passport, plus written consent from any parent who is not traveling. Border officials do ask for these.

faq.question: Is Namibia good for self-driving?
faq.answer: Excellent — it is the classic self-drive safari country, with safe towns and well-marked routes. Respect the gravel: keep speeds down, carry water and spares, refuel whenever you can, and avoid driving after dark.
